//: Assertions are a RATCHET, not a wish.
The first time this ran it asserted performance >= 0.9, because that is
what the README had been claiming since the site existed. It scored 0.57,
and PageSpeed Insights against the live site agreed exactly — so it was
the site, not the runner.
Lowering the threshold to match and calling it green would be worse than
having no check at all: a number nobody can fail is a number nobody reads.
So the floor sits just under the current score, where it stops a
regression, and the goal is written down next to it where it stops being
forgotten. Every time the score moves up, the floor moves up with it.
It moved after CI #8 measured 59 and again after audit run 33356528193
measured a 60 median: 0.55 -> 0.57 -> 0.58. That is the ratchet working;
it does not go back down.
SEVEN RUNS, NOT THREE, AND THAT IS WHY.
This runner is very noisy on this page. One audit produced desktop scores
of 38, 60 and 60 — a 22-point spread inside a single run — and CI #20
measured 54 desktop and 68 mobile off a commit whose only site change was
three statements in an error handler. Neither of those is the site moving.
With three samples a median can sit on a single bad trace, so a floor set
from one median fails against the next one for no reason anybody can act
on. A check that goes red at random gets ignored, and an ignored check is
the thing this repository keeps having to fix.
So the samples went up and the floor stayed where it was. Lowering 0.58 to
match a noisy 54 would have been the easy version and the wrong one: the
measurement was unreliable, not the bar.
What costs the score is total blocking time, and this comment used to say
the cause was building the particle field and the instanced stage on the
main thread. Timed, that is about 2 ms. The cost is GPU work at load —
creating WebGL contexts and compiling shaders. See PERFORMANCE.md, and
tools/medir-arranque.js if you would rather not take its word for it.
Paint is fast: FCP and LCP both land at 0.7s and CLS at 0.05. Those three
are asserted at values the site already meets, so making the score better
cannot come from making the loading worse.
